hints: Focus on what the pH tells you, an oxide that gives a very low pH in water must be strongly acidic, so think about which side of the Periodic Table makes acidic oxides.
Recall that Group 1 metals make basic oxides while non-metals in Groups 14 to 16 make acidic oxides, so eliminate the metal first.
Now compare the non-metals for readiness to burn in air and strength of the acid formed, phosphorus(V) oxide gives strong phosphoric acid while carbon and silicon oxides are much weaker or insoluble.
walkthrough:
**Decode the pH clue**

Great start, let's read what the question is really telling us. A solution of very low pH means a strong acid.

That tells us the oxide of Q must be an acidic, non-metal oxide:
$$\text{non-metal oxide} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{acidic solution}$$

**Use position to predict oxide type**

Remember this lovely pattern. Metals on the left make basic oxides, non-metals on the right make acidic oxides.

So Group 1 (like lithium) gives $\text{Li}_2\text{O}$ which reacts to give $\text{LiOH}$, an alkali of high pH, not low pH.

**Check readiness to oxidise and acid strength**

Now look at the non-metals. Element Q readily oxidises in air, so it must burn easily.

Phosphorus in Period 3, Group 15 does exactly this:
$$\text{P}_4 + 5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$$
$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$
Phosphoric acid is a relatively strong acid, giving very low pH. This fits perfectly.

options.A: Period 2, Group 1 is lithium, a reactive metal. It does oxidise readily, but its oxide $\text{Li}_2\text{O}$ is basic and forms $\text{LiOH}$ in water with high pH (around 13-14), the opposite of what is described.
options.B: Period 2, Group 14 is carbon. Its oxide $\text{CO}_2$ does form a weakly acidic solution (carbonic acid, $\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$), but carbon does not readily oxidise in air at room temperature and the pH is only mildly acidic (about 5-6), not very low.
options.C: Period 3, Group 14 is silicon. Silicon does not readily burn in air, and its oxide $\text{SiO}_2$ is insoluble in water so it does not form an acidic solution at all. This is a trap if you only remember that Group 14 oxides are acidic.
options.D: Period 3, Group 15 is phosphorus. White phosphorus readily oxidises in air to $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, which reacts vigorously with water to give phosphoric acid $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$, a solution of very low pH. Both clues match perfectly.
